11 A uniform rod of length 200 cm is freely pivoted at point P. The rod is held horizontally in
equilibrium by a 60 N weight that is attached to the rod by a string passing over a frictionless
pulley.
frictionless
pulley
uniform rod
40 cm
30°
P
200 cm
weight
60 N
What is the weight of the rod?
A
30 N
B
60 N
C
80 N
D
140 N

hints: Notice P is 40 cm from the left end of the 200 cm rod, so the centre of the uniform rod is 60 cm to the right of P while the string pulls at 160 cm to the right of P.
Connect the 60 N tension at $30^{\circ}$ to the rod to its vertical part $60 \sin 30^{\circ}$, because only the perpendicular distance from the horizontal rod gives a moment about P.
Set clockwise moment from the rod weight equal to anticlockwise moment from that vertical component about P, then solve for the rod weight.
walkthrough: Find the moment arms about P. Rod length is 200 cm with P 40 cm from the left, so the right end is $200 - 40 = 160 \text{ cm}$ from P. The uniform rod weight $W$ acts at its midpoint 100 cm from the left, so $100 - 40 = 60 \text{ cm}$ to the right of P.

Find the upward force at the right end. The frictionless pulley transmits the 60 N tension, acting at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. Its vertical component is $F = 60 \sin 30^{\circ} = 60 \times 0.5 = 30 \text{ N}$ upward.

Apply the principle of moments about P for equilibrium. The rod weight tends to turn the rod one way and the $30 \text{ N}$ upward pull tends to turn it the opposite way, so $\text{sum of moments about P} = 0$.
Substitute with units: $W \times 60 \text{ cm} = 30 \text{ N} \times 160 \text{ cm}$.
Solve: $W = 30 \times 160 / 60 = 4800 / 60 = 80 \text{ N}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: 30 N is the vertical component $60 \sin 30^{\circ}$ of the string tension, not the rod weight after taking moments about P.

B.explanation: 60 N ignores both the $30^{\circ}$ angle and the different moment arms of 60 cm and 160 cm about P.

C.explanation: Moments about P balance when $W \times 60 = 60\sin 30^{\circ} \times 160$, giving $W = 80 \text{ N}$.

D.explanation: 140 N would result from using the full 60 N tension vertically or adding forces instead of equating clockwise and anticlockwise moments.
